------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ Jyotsna Rewal Dua, Judge
The petitioner seeks compensation in lieu of his land utilized by the respondents for constructing a
road.

2. From the conjoint reading of the pleadings, following facts emerge:-
2(i).

The case of the petitioner is that his father late Sh. Padam Chand was recorded owner in possession of the land comprised in Khata Khatauni No.3 Min, Khasra No.160, measuring 00-13-24 hectares, situated at Mauja Dhara, Tehsil Rohru,
District Shimla, as per the Jamabandi 1
Whether reporters of print and electronic media may be allowed to see the order?

Yes.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Petitioner and other legal heirs succeeded to the estate of Sh. Padam Chand on his demise.
Their names were entered in the subsequent Jamabandi for the year 2013-14.

Present petition has been filed by the .
petitioner on his own behalf and for the benefit of other legal heirs of late Sh. Padam Chand.

The respondents carried out construction work of Dhara-Shekhal road in Tehsil Rohru,
District Shimla.
According to the petitioner, despite the objections of the petitioner and other stakeholders, the land in question though utilized by the respondents for constructing the road, but was not acquired.
The road was constructed without paying any compensation to the land owners.
2(iii).

Further case of the petitioner is that different notifications under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act were issued by the respondents on different dates, i.e. 14.05.2007, 24.07.2007,
05.04.2008 and 07.07.2009.
These notifications pertained to some land parcels utilized by the respondents for construction of Dhara-Shekhal road.
Notification under Section 4 was not issued for the land owned by late Sh. Padam Chand.
The respondents completed the acquisition process of some portions of the land utilized for construction of the said road.

Following awards were eventually passed in respect of some land parcels covered under the road:-
"i) Award No.48/08 Passed on 03.10.2008 ii) Award No.33/2008 Passed on 23.10.2008 iii) Award No.58/2008 Passed on 22.10.2008 .
iv) Award No.47/2008 Passed on 03.10.2008 v) Award No.8/2010 Passed on 19.04.2010 vi) Award No.58/11 Passed on 31.10.2011."
2(iv).
The grievance of the petitioner is that despite his repeated requests, land owned by his father late Sh. Padam Chand, utilized by the respondents for construction of the road has not been acquired.

No compensation in lieu thereof has been paid to the successors-in-interest of late Sh.
Padam Chand.

Ramesh Kumar vs State Of H.P. And Others on 13 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71498448/
2 3.

entities.text: Ramesh Kumar vs State Of H.P. And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The respondents in their reply have not denied utilizing the land in question for construction of Dhara- Shekhal road.
According to the respondents, the road was constructed during the year 1996-97 on the persistent demand of the residents of the area including the petitioner/his predecessor-in-interest.
The respondents have also admitted that different notifications under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act were issued by them in respect of some of the land parcels covered by the road in question.

It has also been admitted that the awards as mentioned by the petitioner in the writ petition were passed by the respondents in respect of few of the land parcels utilized for construction of the road.

However, according to the respondents, this was done "only as per direction of Hon'ble Court under compelling circumstances as the judgments passed in different matters by the Hon'ble courts .
attained finality".
The respondents have mainly contested the petition on account of alleged delay on part of the petitioner in taking legal recourse as also on account of alleged estoppel against him.
According to the respondents, the petitioner/his predecessor-in-interest alongwith other residents of the area had voluntarily offered their lands for availing the road connectivity.
The land owners including the petitioner/his predecessor-in-interest did not raise any objection/demand for compensation of the land.
As per the respondents, the petition filed after an inordinate delay of 25 years from the date of construction of the road is only an attempt to receive undue benefit from the respondents.
4. I have heard learned counsel for the parties.

In my considered view, for the following reasons, the petitioner has made out a case in his favour:-
4(i).
It is an admitted position that the land in question owned by the petitioner/his predecessor-in- interest has been utilized by the respondents for construction of Dhara-Shekhali road.

The respondents have also not denied that pursuant to the directions issued by this Court, lands of some of the land owners falling under the road in question were acquired by them under award Nos.48/2008, 33/2008, 58/2008, 47/2008, 8/2010 and .
58/2011, announced on different dates.

It is not the case of the respondents that they were prohibited from acquiring the land of other affected land owners including the petitioner/legal heirs of late Sh. Padam Chand, whose lands were also utilized for the construction of that very road.
4(ii).
Respondent is a welfare State.

Once the lands of some of the land owners utilized for construction of the road in question had been acquired, it was incumbent upon them to have given the same treatment to the petitioner, whose land was also utilized for construction of that very road.

Ramesh Kumar vs State Of H.P. And Others on 13 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71498448/
3 4(iii).

It would also be appropriate to refer to a recent judgment passed by the Division Bench of this Court on 28.06.2023 in CWP No.6581/2021 (Labdhu Ram Vs.
State of H.P. & Ors).

CWP No.6581/2021 (Labdhu Ram Vs.
State of H.P. & Ors)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The petitioner therein had raised a factual plea that though certain others, whose lands were utilized for the road, were paid the compensation,
but he was denied the same even though his land was also utilized for construction of same road.
Road in that case was laid in the year 1995-96.
Taking note of various pronouncements, viz. (1986) 2 SCC 68 (State of Himachal Pradesh Vs Umeed Ram Sharma), (2016) 7 SCC 498 (Swaraj Abhiyan(I) vs. Union of India and ors.), (2020) 9 SCC .

Ravichandra and Ors Vs. Union of India & Ors.), (2022) 7 SCC 508 (Sukh Dutt Ratra & Anr. Vs. State of Himachal Pradesh & Ors.), the contention of delay and laches raised by the respondents-State was turned down.

entities.text: Sukh Dutt Ratra & Anr. Vs. State of Himachal Pradesh & Ors.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The observations of the Hon'ble Apex Court that the State cannot evade its legal responsibility towards those from whom private property has been expropriated, were reiterated.

It will be appropriate to extract following paragraphs from Labdhu Ram's case (supra):-
"18.
In Sukh Dutt Ratra, supra, the appellant's land had been utilized for construction of road in 1972-73 without initiating any proceedings for acquisition and without paying any compensation.

When the petitioner filed a writ petition on the basis of relief granted to other owners whose land was so acquired, the said Writ petition was dismissed by the High Court holding that there were disputed questions of law and fact for determination on the starting point of limitation, which cannot be adjudicated in the writ proceeding and the petitioners were given liberty to approach the Civil Court.

The Supreme Court reversed the said decision and held that nobody can be deprived of liberty or property without due process, or authorization of law and the State has a higher responsibility in demonstrating that it has acted within the confines of legality, and had not tarnished the basic principle of the rule of law.

It held that State, merely on the ground of delay and laches, cannot evade its legal responsibility .
towards those from whom private property has been expropriated.

It observed that the State was initiating acquisition proceedings selectively and not in every case like that of the appellants whose land was taken, and at every stage it sought to shirk its responsibility of acquiring land required for public use in the manner prescribed by law.
Ramesh Kumar vs State Of H.P. And Others on 13 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71498448/
4

entities.text: Ramesh Kumar vs State Of H.P. And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It held that the State cannot shield itself behind the ground of delay and laches in such a situation as there cannot be a limitation to doing justice.

It also rejected the plea alleged verbal consent or lack of objection on the ground that no material was placed on record to substantiate the said plea and held that the State was unable to produce any evidence indicating that the land of the appellant had been taken over or acquired in the manner known to law, or that it had ever paid any compensation.
It declared that there is no period of limitation prescribed for the courts to exercise their constitutional jurisdiction to do substantial justice.
It directed the State to treat the subject land as a deemed acquisition and disburse compensation to the appellants therein in terms of similar orders passed in other cases within four months.

19. In view of the above settled legal position, we are of the opinion that the stand of the State that it need not pay any compensation for utilizing the petitioner's land for the purpose of laying a road cannot be countenanced and the State is bound to pay market value compensation to the petitioner for utilizing his land for the purpose of the road.

20. Therefore, the writ petition is allowed with costs of Rs.10,000/- and a direction is issued to the respondents to demarcate the land of the petitioner utilized for the purpose of the road in question within four weeks, treat it as having been acquired for the said purpose and pay him the highest amount towards compensation among compensation under the awards Annexures P-3 and P-4 with all statutory benefits under the Land Acquisition Act,1894 within eight weeks."
The ratio of the aforesaid judgment squarely applies to the facts of the instant case as well.

In the instant case also, the land of the petitioner/legal heirs of late Sh. Padam Chand had .
admittedly been utilized for construction of the road, but neither the same has been acquired nor any compensation has been paid to the petitioner/legal heirs of late Sh. Padam Chand.

Some of the other land owners whose lands have been utilized for construction of the same road have been awarded compensation vide Award Nos.48/2008, 33/2008, 58/2008, 47/2008, 8/2010 and 58/2011, announced on different dates.

Petitioner is similarly situated vis--vis the land owners in whose cases the awards were passed by the respondents for acquisition of the land for constructing the road in question.
5.
In the given facts and circumstances of the case and in light of the legal position, this writ petition is allowed.

The respondents are directed to demarcate the land of the petitioner/legal heirs of late Sh. Padam Chand utilized for construction of the road in question and such land be treated to have been acquired for the said purpose in accordance with law.

Respondents are further directed to pay the highest amount towards compensation to the petitioner under the aforesaid awards with all Ramesh Kumar vs State Of H.P. And Others on 13 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71498448/
5 statutory benefits under the Land Acquisition Act.
